from cache import make_key
from service import score

def test_cache_invalidation():
    store = {}
    compute_calls = []
    def compute():
        compute_calls.append(len(compute_calls))
        return f'val{len(compute_calls)}'
    
    job_text = 'job1'
    profile_version = 'prof1'
    criteria_version = 'c1'
    criteria_version2 = 'c2'
    
    # first call
    val1 = score(store, job_text, profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    assert val1 == 'val1'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 1
    
    # change job_text only
    val2 = score(store, 'job2', profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    assert val2 == 'val2'  # new compute call expected
    assert len(compute_calls) == 2
    
    # change profile only
    val3 = score(store, job_text, 'prof2', criteria_version, compute)
    assert val3 == 'val3'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 3
    
    # change criteria only
    val4 = score(store, job_text, profile_version, criteria_version2, compute)
    assert val4 == 'val4'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 4
    
    # all same as first call
    val5 = score(store, job_text, profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    assert val5 == 'val1'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 4  # reuse cache
    
    # all same as second call (job2, prof1, c1)
    val6 = score(store, 'job2', profile_version, criteria_version, compute)
    assert val6 == 'val2'
    assert len(compute_calls) == 4  # reuse cache

def test_make_key_unambiguous():
    key1 = make_key('t', 'p', 'c')
    key2 = make_key('t', 'p', 'c2')
    key3 = make_key('t2', 'p', 'c')
    key4 = make_key('t', 'p2', 'c')
    key5 = make_key('t', 'p', 'c')
    
    # all distinct when inputs differ
    assert key1 != key2
    assert key1 != key3
    assert key1 != key4
    assert key1 == key5
    # key is a tuple, no ambiguous concatenation
    assert isinstance(key1, tuple)
    assert len(key1) == 3

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_make_key_unambiguous()
    test_cache_invalidation()
    print('All tests passed')

turns.report: Changed cache.py make_key to return (text, profile, criteria) tuple ensuring all three inputs affect caching uniquely. Created candidate_tests.py with tests verifying cache invalidation on any input change and key unambiguity. All tests passed.
